events.label: founding
events.text: Meeting in Paris voted the Union Académique Internationale into existence, CVA's parent body.

evidence.quote: He called a meeting of representatives from any interested academies in Paris for May , 1919
The meetings in 1919 were foundation meetings

events.label: bylaws
events.text: Union bylaws were passed at a second meeting.

evidence.quote: At a second meeting in October , bylaws were passed

events.text: Union moved to Brussels, where the General Secretariat was seated.

evidence.quote: after which the Union moved to Brussels

events.label: assembly
events.text: First assembly of the academies of the Union held.

evidence.quote: The first assembly of the academies was not until 1920

events.text: First CVA fascicle for the Louvre published.

evidence.quote: He was also the publisher of the first fascicle for the Louvre in 1922

events.text: CVA descriptions and images made freely accessible as web database, CVA Online.

evidence.quote: Since 2004 all textual descriptions and images are freely accessible as a web-based database

events.text: Austrian commission first used a 3D scanner for CVA vessel shape documentation.

evidence.quote: The Austrian commission used for the first-time of the CVA project a 3D-Scanner for documentation of vessel shapes in 2006

events.text: Renderings with rollouts shown at the Louvre in the 100 years CVA exhibition.

evidence.quote: In the second half of 2019 rendings
including rollouts were shown at the Louvre as part of the 100 years CVA exhibition

undated_mentions: Henri Pirenne elected president of the Union
Five projects proposed for the Union; three voted, Project Number 1 being the Corpus Vasorum Antiquorum
Final decision to publish a comprehensive catalogue of painted ancient Greek vases
Follow-up 3D-acquisition project granted and a second 3D-technology volume published
Juliette de La Genière currently in charge of the Union's patronage
